hero.caption: The Irish National Botanic Gardens, Glasnevin, Dublin, Ireland. The Curvilinear Range of Glasshouses at the national Botanic Gardens were constructed between 1843 and 1869 and designed by native Dubliner Richard Turner. He was also responsible for designing the Glasshouse at Kew Gardens (England) and Belfast (N. Ireland) but both of these have been 'restored' with the use of steel. The Curvilinear Range was restored in 1995 with repairs carried out in the original wrought iron. Internally the houses feel amazingly light and even though, slim and elegant, much of the structure had decorative elements.

images.filename: Glasnevin Jct, Dublin - geograph.org.uk - 1084461.jpg
images.caption: Glasnevin Junction, Dublin, Ireland. Glasnevin Junction is where the line from Islandbridge Junction (west of Dublin Heuston station 375413) joins the line (left) from Sligo to Dublin Connolly station via North Strand Jct. The train is a goods transfer (mostly Guinness kegs) from Heuston to the North Wall goods yard, hauled by CIÉ 141 Class diesel locomotive 162.

images.caption: Sligo train at Glasnevin JunctionA CIE 001 class locomotive takes the 07.30 Sligo - Dublin passenger train over Glasnevin Junction.
